summary: Contractor conversion to FTE: laptop ownership, service-account consolidation and KMS key handoff policy question
description:
Issue summary:
A contractor (SaaS Integrations team) has accepted a full-time offer. HR requests guidance and execution on three interdependent items before the official start date: (1) confirm laptop ownership transfer vs. return/reissue; (2) consolidate two temporary service accounts created during the contract into a single FTE service identity and migrate permissions; (3) transfer access to an internal dataset encrypted with a customer-specific KMS key currently accessible via the contractor's service account.

Impact:
- Delay in start date or onboarding tasks if hardware and credentials are not resolved.
- Potential security/compliance risk if KMS key access is not properly re-scoped.
- Engineering productivity hit if service account consolidation breaks CI jobs the contractor authored.

Background and constraints:
- Contractor used a loaner company laptop (Asset tag: L-90173) assigned by HW team on 2024-11-18. Contract policy historically required return, but a recent HR memo allowed asset transfers in special cases after lead approval.
- Two temporary service accounts exist: svc-temp-integ-901 and svc-temp-data-901. Both have been used in development and a staging CI workflow. svc-temp-data-901 has decrypt access tied to kms-customer-42 key via a role binding.
- Contractor will transition teams on day 1 as an FTE and needs continuity for certain development workflows.

Requested outcomes (by HR + Eng manager):
1) Clear decision and documented approval for laptop: transfer ownership to employee vs. collect and reissue a fresh asset.
2) Plan and execute service account consolidation (create svc-fte-901), migrate permissions and update any references in infra/CI, with a rollback plan.
3) Re-scope KMS access so that svc-fte-901 holds the necessary decrypt permissions and revoke svc-temp-data-901. All changes must be auditable.

Timeline: HR requests completion before official start date 2026-03-18.

Stakeholders: HR (Alyssa Green), Eng Manager (Rohan Mehta), Contractor / new FTE (Jordan Reyes), Security (Priya Menon), IT Hardware (Luis Ortega), SRE (assigned: Ethan Zhang).

Acceptance criteria:
- Asset ownership recorded in inventory with transfer approval log.
- svc-fte-901 provisioned and in use; all CI references tested in staging and production-safe branch.
- KMS policy updated and validated, old service accounts revoked and audit entries captured.

Additional notes: Please coordinate a short blackout window for CI deployments if migration involves infra changes. If policy requires legal sign-off for asset transfer, loop Legal early.

investigation_notes: Inventory check: L-90173 shows loaner state; last checkout user = Jordan Reyes. IAM audit (2026-03-10) shows svc-temp-data-901 performed 5 decrypt ops in last 30 days. Reviewed CI references: two pipelines in infra repo refer to svc-temp-integ-901 and one scheduler job uses svc-temp-data-901. Security flagged kms-customer-42 policy as customer-specific; change requires update to key policy and a documented key policy change request. No evidence of external access or compromise.
resolution_notes: Work in progress. Interim workaround: IT issued a short-term personal laptop mapping for Jordan to avoid startup delays if inventory transfer is delayed. Drafted svc-fte-901 and tested permission grant in a staging namespace; pending final KMS policy update and HR form upload. Plan: 1) HR signs transfer form (expected 2026-03-12). 2) Security approves key policy change (expected 2026-03-13). 3) Migration to staging on 2026-03-16, production migration after validation. Rollback: re-enable svc-temp-* accounts and revert IAM bindings within a 1-hour window.
notes: Legal consulted and confirmed not required for this low-value asset per HR memo (ref in Confluence). Ensure audit trail captured before revoking old service-account keys.
